classification.difficultyReason: Select familiar cyclic supplements, same-arc equalities and diameter rightangles, then link a few angle-sum steps including an intersecting-diagonal sector; all constructions and theorems are supplied.

content.prompt: Find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$, giving reasons.

spec.description: Cyclic quadrilateral C B D A. ∠CBD = 100°; θ = ∠CAD.

answer.worked: Opposite angles in cyclic quadrilateral CBDA are supplementary, so $\theta=180^\circ-100^\circ=80^\circ$.

answer.worked: Opposite angles in cyclic ABCD are supplementary: $\alpha=180^\circ-80^\circ=100^\circ$ and $\beta=180^\circ-85^\circ=95^\circ$.

spec.description: Cyclic quadrilateral A B C D with diagonals AC and BD. ∠ABD = 45°; ∠DBC = 40°, indicated by an external leader. The upper-right angle between BD and AC at their unlabelled intersection is 80°. α = ∠CAD; β = ∠ACD; γ = ∠ADB; θ = ∠BDC.
spec.mathematics: All original source vertices/chords/diameters/parallel/equality/angle sectors preserved. Metric realization adds no numeric datum. Label guides .4pt, no paint masks.
spec.answerVisibility: Original givens and requested Greek labels only; no computed answers in student figure.

answer.worked: Same-arc angles give $\alpha=\angle DBC=40^\circ$ and $\beta=\angle ABD=45^\circ$. Let E be the unlabelled intersection of AC and BD. The given exterior angle BEC is $80^\circ$, so in triangle CDE, $80^\circ=\beta+\theta$, giving $\theta=35^\circ$. In triangle ACD, the angle at D is $\gamma+\theta$. Thus $40^\circ+45^\circ+\gamma+35^\circ=180^\circ$, so $\gamma=60^\circ$.

spec.description: Cyclic quadrilateral P Q R S with diagonal PR. Actual upper small P-sector QPR is20degrees, indicated by an external leader; lower sector RPS is40degrees. Angle PQR is130degrees via external leader. Alpha=PSR,beta=PRS,gamma=QRP. Preserve literal original20/40 givens and their actual sectors; prior inventory reversed the two wedge descriptions.

answer.worked: The original upper P-sector QPR is $20^\circ$ and lower RPS is $40^\circ$. Opposite cyclic angles give $\alpha=180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ$. Triangle PRS gives $\beta=180^\circ-40^\circ-50^\circ=90^\circ$. Triangle PQR gives $\gamma=180^\circ-130^\circ-20^\circ=30^\circ$.

spec.description: Cyclic quadrilateral C D A B. BA extends through A to X; CB extends through B to Y. Exterior ∠DAX = 70°; exterior ∠ABY = 100°. α = ∠DAB; β = ∠CBA; γ = ∠BCD; θ = ∠CDA.

answer.worked: Straight angles at A and B give $\alpha=180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ$ and $\beta=180^\circ-100^\circ=80^\circ$. Opposite cyclic angles are supplementary, so $\gamma=180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ$ and $\theta=180^\circ-80^\circ=100^\circ$.

spec.description: Circle with diameter JM through marked centreO, with J,K,L,M along the upper semicircle and chords JK,KL,LM,JL,KM. Given angleJMK20degrees. Alpha=KLJ via external leader,beta=JLM,gamma=JKM. Theta is the WHOLE angleKJM: the source theta arc runs from JM to JK across internal JL, not merely LJM. No given or original arc changed; prior inventory misidentified theta terminal ray.

answer.worked: Angles KLJ and KMJ stand on arc KJ, so $\alpha=20^\circ$. Since JM is a diameter, $\beta=\angle JLM=90^\circ$ and $\gamma=\angle JKM=90^\circ$ by Thales. The source theta arc is the whole angle KJM across internal JL. In triangle JKM, $\theta=180^\circ-90^\circ-20^\circ=70^\circ$.
